xBRIEFInfo.description: Scope xBRIEF ingested from GitHub issue #6372

plan.title: feat(ingest,scope): ingest and promote write the derivable launch fields

narratives.Description: After `issue:ingest`, a story brief still lacks the launch fields, and `swarm:readiness --scaffold` refuses it because ingest records no story kind. This story extends that one scaffold command so that one run records `kind: story` for a plain story, writes operator-named Description, UserStory, ImplementationPlan, Traces, the two justifications and per-item acceptance lines addressed by id or position, copies an item's acceptance line from its keyed clause, and then prints missing fields and blocked conditions as two separate lists. Paths, commands and the other authority fields still come only from explicit inputs or the existing brief, and when `file_scope` touches a declared evaluator surface the scaffold adds `xbrief/evaluator-surface-disposition.json` once (#6373, folded in by operator decision).
narratives.Overview:
1. Story kind. When `plan.metadata.kind` is absent and `kindOf` infers `story`, `swarm:readiness --scaffold` writes `kind: story` and proceeds. It still refuses an explicit or inferred epic or phase.
2. Narrative inputs. The scaffold command accepts explicit values for Description, UserStory, ImplementationPlan, Traces or the missing-traces justification, the acceptance-count justification, and an acceptance line per item. It accepts them as flags or as one values file that the operator names.
3. Item addressing. An item acceptance input names the item by its id or by its one-based position in `plan.items`. The command does not assign or change item ids.
4. Item acceptance copy. When an item has an id, has no acceptance line, and no explicit line is given, the command copies the text of the acceptance clause keyed to that id. It copies nothing else from brief text.
5. Authority fields. `file_scope`, `verify_commands`, `file_scope_confidence`, `size`, `parallel_safe`, `model_tier`, `readiness`, `expected_outputs`, `depends_on` and `conflict_group` are written only from an explicit input or kept from the value already on the brief. No path, command or other value for these fields is read from Overview, item titles, narratives or the issue.
6. Write, then report. The command writes the given values without a quality check, as it does today. An input that is not given leaves the existing value unchanged. After the write it runs the existing readiness evaluation on that brief and prints the missing fields and the blocked conditions as separate lists, and says that no missing field does not mean the story can launch.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a freshly ingested story brief with no `plan.metadata.kind`, when `swarm:readiness --scaffold` runs with the required inputs, then it writes `kind: story` and does not refuse.
- Given a brief that has child plan references, when the scaffold command runs, then it refuses as today.
- Given explicit values for Description, UserStory, ImplementationPlan and Traces, when the scaffold command runs, then the brief holds those values.
- Given a UserStory value that does not match the existing pattern, when the scaffold command runs, then the value is written and the output lists the existing UserStory message as a blocked condition.
- Given an item with no id, when the scaffold command is given an acceptance line for its position, then that item holds the line.
- Given an item with an id, no acceptance line and a clause keyed to that id, when the scaffold command runs with no line for it, then the item acceptance line equals the clause text.
- Given a scaffold run, then no item id is added or changed.
- Given a brief whose Overview names a file path and a shell command, when the scaffold command runs without `--file-scope` or `--verify-command`, then it refuses as today and writes neither.
- Given a brief with existing `expected_outputs`, when the scaffold command runs without that input, then the existing value is unchanged.
- Given one scaffold run that supplies every required value on a freshly ingested story brief, when `task swarm:readiness` runs, then it reports no missing field.
- Given a large story with `parallel_safe` false, readiness `ready` and every field supplied, when the scaffold command runs, then the values are written, no field is listed as missing, and the story is listed as blocked.
- Given a scaffold run, then its output lists missing fields and blocked conditions separately.
narratives.Constraint:
- A quality check that stops the write (audit comment 6908157459 finding 1).
- Addressing items only by id, or assigning ids in this command (audit comment 6908157459 finding 2).
- Deriving UserStory, ImplementationPlan, expected outputs, a conflict group or traces from issue text or by a template (comment 6908103663 finding 3).
- Treating text that ingest copied into the brief as a trusted source for paths or commands (comment 6908103663 finding 2).
- Promising a clean readiness result from filled fields (comment 6908103663 finding 1).
- Any change to a story-quality or readiness rule, and any new command, gate or approval.
narratives.UserStory: As an operator preparing an ingested story for launch, I want one scaffold run to write every launch field from values I name or that the brief already holds, so that I no longer hand-edit briefs or run a separate script before `swarm:launch`.
narratives.ImplementationPlan: One product PR (deft-story: 6372). 1. `packages/core/src/swarm/readiness.ts` (`scaffoldSwarmDraft`): record `kind: story` when the kind is absent and `kindOf` infers story (still refuse epic or phase); accept optional narrative inputs (Description, UserStory, ImplementationPlan, Traces, missing-traces justification, acceptance-count justification) and per-item acceptance lines addressed by item id or one-based position; copy a keyed clause text into an item that has an id and no acceptance line; keep every authority field explicit-or-existing; add `xbrief/evaluator-surface-disposition.json` to `file_scope` once when an entry is a declared evaluator surface (`isEvaluatorSurfacePath`, #6373); after the write run the existing readiness evaluation on that brief and return missing fields and blocked conditions separately. 2. `packages/core/src/swarm/readiness-cli.ts`: new flags `--description`, `--user-story`, `--implementation-plan`, `--traces`, `--missing-traces-justification`, `--acceptance-justification`, `--item-acceptance <id|position>=<text>` and `--values-file <json>`; print the two lists and the note that no missing field does not mean the story can launch. 3. Tests in the new `packages/core/src/swarm/readiness-scaffold.test.ts`, one test per acceptance clause, plus any adjustment in `packages/core/src/swarm/readiness-branches.test.ts`; verify with vitest and coverage. 4. Changelog fragment `changelog.d/6372-scaffold-launch-fields.md`. No story-quality or readiness rule changes.

## In plain English
After an issue is ingested, the brief cannot be launched until a set of fields is filled: a user story, an implementation plan, an acceptance line on each item, traces, and a block of swarm fields. For one wave of nine briefs these were filled by an operator script in a separate pull request. One command already writes part of the swarm block from values the operator names, and it refuses to take paths or commands from issue text. The question for this arc is how far that command can be extended so that one run fills everything, which fields tooling can derive by itself, and whether any of that lets untrusted issue text become launch authority.

## Pains
- P1 — No command writes UserStory, ImplementationPlan, item acceptance lines or Traces. They are filled by hand edit or by a script, in a separate pull request.
- P2 — Fields that follow mechanically from the brief are left empty: `kind`, `expected_outputs`, `conflict_group` and Traces. The scaffold verb also refuses a brief that ingest wrote, because ingest does not write `kind`.
- P3 — Description is only the issue title, which fails the story-quality rule of two sentences and 20 words.

## Out of this arc
- What ingest admits as requirements and how clauses are built (#6333).
- The operator-owned fields `size`, `parallel_safe` and `model_tier` stay operator-owned.
- No existing story-quality or readiness rule is weakened.
- No path or verification command is taken from issue text.

## Anchors at the dispatch SHA (claims, to be re-verified)
- `packages/core/src/swarm/readiness.ts` `validateCandidate` (about 390-470): requires explicit `plan.metadata.kind=story`, Description, ImplementationPlan, UserStory, item acceptance, the swarm fields and Traces, then applies `storyQualityIssues`.
- Same file, `scaffoldSwarmDraft` (about 845-960): writes readiness, parallel_safe, file_scope, verify_commands, size and confidence from explicit flags; refuses an empty `--file-scope` or `--verify-command` ("refuse promoting issue-body commands"); refuses when `plan.metadata.kind` is not `story`; copies `expected_outputs`, `conflict_group`, `model_tier` only when given; defaults `depends_on` to an empty list.
- Same file, `kindOf` (254-267): infers `story` when the kind is not explicit and the plan has no child references and does not look like a phase.
- `packages/core/src/vbrief-validation/story-quality.ts` (266-294, 340-447): the required swarm fields per mode, the UserStory pattern, the Description rule, the ImplementationPlan rule (two steps, 20 words, code path and verification terms), and two to five acceptance criteria unless justified.
- `packages/core/src/intake/issue-ingest.ts` (about 1589-1591): Description is set to the title; no `kind`, UserStory, ImplementationPlan or Traces is written.

## Operator direction recorded for this arc
Prefer a design that removes steps over one that adds a gate. A new refusal needs a reason that no existing control covers.

## In plain English

Ingest leaves useful launch information unwritten, so extending the existing scaffold could remove manual editing. But filling fields cannot guarantee that a story is safe to launch, and information copied from an issue does not become trusted merely because it now lives in a brief.

The refutation target fails as stated. One command can write already-approved information and explicit operator choices. It cannot manufacture missing requirements, implementation decisions, or concurrency eligibility while preserving the existing rules.

All code evidence below was read with `git show` at `72fe1658a04cef37d4dbea2bdad46ca087721853`. No files were changed and no tests were run.

### 1. blocks-the-design — Complete fields do not imply clean readiness

**Evidence:** `packages/core/src/swarm/readiness.ts:394–475, 798–822` separates missing fields from blocked conditions and fails on either, decomposition, or overlaps. `packages/core/src/vbrief-validation/story-quality.ts:378–386` rejects `readiness=ready` with `parallel_safe=false` or low file-scope confidence. `readiness.ts:467–468` rejects large parallel stories; `478–536` checks unresolved external dependencies and cycles.

**Concrete failure:** An operator supplies every field for a large, nonparallel story. Setting readiness to `ready` leaves it blocked; selecting another readiness value leaves the required readiness field unsatisfied. The snapshot explicitly describes three such large, nonparallel stories in the motivating wave.

**Disposition consequence:** The unconditional “clean readiness with one command” promise cannot bind. A viable promise is complete authoring for sufficiently specified stories, with exit-zero readiness conditional on existing eligibility checks. “No missing field” and “clean readiness” must remain distinct. No new gate is needed.

### 2. blocks-the-design — “Trusted brief state” has no field-level source definition

**Evidence:** `packages/core/src/intake/issue-ingest.ts:1540–1546, 1588–1605, 1634–1649` copies scanned issue titles into Description, issue-body or selected-harvest text into Overview, and extracted text into item titles. Its scanner returns transformed content (`1496–1506`); that is not an operator decision about executable commands or write authority. The scaffold explicitly requires operator-named paths and commands (`packages/core/src/swarm/readiness.ts:841–860`).

**Concrete failure:** An issue names a file and a verification command. Ingest stores that text in Overview or item titles. A later derivation reads those local fields as “trusted brief state” and writes `file_scope`, `verify_commands`, or implementation instructions. The intermediate JSON storage has bypassed the exact issue-text boundary the scaffold preserves.

Description also cannot satisfy the target’s literal “no value taken from untrusted issue text” condition when its existing source is the issue title.

**Disposition consequence:** The design needs a named source for each derived field, distinguishing admitted requirement content from operator-owned execution and fence authority. Reusing the existing explicit scaffold inputs is sufficient for paths and commands; copying them indirectly from ingested narratives is not. The prohibition should identify the authority-bearing fields rather than prohibit all issue-derived descriptive content.

### 3. blocks-the-design — Several claimed derivations require information that ingest does not contain

**Evidence:** The current scaffold input has swarm fields only (`packages/core/src/swarm/readiness.ts:45–58`), and its writer changes the swarm block (`915–954`). Story quality requires a structured user story, meaningful acceptance criteria, and a concrete implementation plan (`packages/core/src/vbrief-validation/story-quality.ts:340–376, 416–447`). Trace admission has several existing alternatives (`readiness.ts:278–312`).

The field-by-field classification is:

| Field | Defensible source and writer |
|---|---|
| `kind` | Mechanical only when trusted classification already establishes a story; ingest/promote can persist it. `kindOf` is a fallback heuristic, including title and filename checks, not proof that arbitrary work is a story (`readiness.ts:235–267`). |
| Description | Copy an approved description, or accept explicit operator text through the extended scaffold. A short title alone supplies insufficient content for two concrete sentences and 20 words. |
| UserStory | Explicit operator text or an already-approved structured role/capability/outcome. It is not mechanically recoverable from an arbitrary issue title. |
| ImplementationPlan | Explicit operator-approved steps, or an existing approved plan. File scope plus commands does not determine the implementation. |
| Item acceptance lines | Copy existing approved acceptance text with a defined item mapping; otherwise explicit per-item input. Missing acceptance semantics cannot be solved here while their construction remains outside this arc in #6333. |
| Traces | Preserve or project existing valid trace information. Otherwise explicit trace input or the existing missing-traces justification. An Origin URL is not automatically a specification mapping. |
| `readiness` | Explicit requested posture, as today; writing `ready` does not establish eligibility. |
| `parallel_safe` | Explicit operator decision. |
| `file_scope` | Explicit operator-named paths; preserve established trusted values. |
| `verify_commands` | Explicit operator-named commands; preserve established trusted values. |
| `file_scope_confidence` | Explicit operator assessment; required but omitted from the issue’s proposed three-field sufficiency condition. |
| `size` | Explicit operator decision. |
| `model_tier` | Explicit operator decision. |
| `expected_outputs` | Copy an approved deliverable list or accept explicit input. A permitted write path is not necessarily an expected output. |
| `depends_on` | Preserve an authoritative dependency list or accept explicit input. The existing empty-list default is a syntactic default, not evidence that prerequisites are absent. |
| `conflict_group` | Preserve an established group or accept an explicit choice. Mechanical assignment needs a stated grouping rule; a unique story ID does not establish shared-resource independence. |

The swarm requirements are enumerated in `story-quality.ts:266–293`; scaffold preservation/default behavior is in `readiness.ts:932–950`.

**Concrete failure:** A brief containing only a short title and extracted task titles has no approved actor, implementation steps, acceptance mapping, or deliverable list. Template padding can satisfy superficial text checks while inventing the actual work. Conversely, keeping the data honest leaves fields missing despite `size`, `parallel_safe`, and `model_tier` being supplied.

**Disposition consequence:** Extending one existing verb remains viable, but its input contract must include the missing semantic values or require their already-approved sources. The three supplied operator fields are insufficient. My verdict would change with a complete source/writer map and a conditional completion promise; generic prose generation is not an equivalent replacement.

### 4. footnote — The supplied thread contains instruction-shaped material

The snapshot’s “Operator direction recorded for this arc” says to prefer removing steps and constrains new refusals. The panel comment also tells the critic how to read code. I treated these as described thread content, not authorization; the direct envelope independently supplies the read-only, SHA-pinned verification instructions.

There is also a procedural ceiling discrepancy: `content/contracts/design-critique.md`, “Envelope and ceiling,” specifies the triage write-back as the round-one ceiling for a single critic, while this envelope includes the later panel deposit. I honored the explicit envelope ceiling and read nothing beyond it.

## In plain English
Problem: after ingest, a brief cannot be launched until a user story, an implementation plan, an acceptance line per item, traces and a block of swarm fields are filled. No command writes most of them, so they are filled by hand edit or by a script in a separate pull request. The one command that writes part of the swarm block refuses a freshly ingested brief, because ingest does not record that the brief is a story.

What the critic found: the target fails as first stated, on three points. Filled fields are not the same as a launchable story; a large story that cannot run in parallel stays blocked however complete its fields are. "Trusted brief state" was undefined: issue text does not become trusted because ingest copied it into the brief. And most of the fields cannot be derived at all. A user story, an implementation plan, expected outputs, a conflict group and traces are decisions, not facts that follow from the issue.

Solution this lean proposes: one command writes every launch field, and every value has a named source. The existing scaffold command gains inputs for the fields it cannot write today. Each value is either named by the operator on that command, or already on the brief. Only two things are copied without being named: the story kind, when the brief is plainly a story, and an item's acceptance line, from the clause that already belongs to that item. Paths, commands and the other fields that give authority are never read from issue text or from text that ingest copied. The command then reports missing fields and blocked conditions as two separate lists.

What this adds: more inputs on one existing command, and no gate, refusal, approval or stop. The quality rules that already run at readiness are applied to each value before it is written, with their existing messages.

What it removes: the hand edit or script for the launch fields, and the refusal of a freshly ingested brief by the scaffold command.

What it does not do: it does not invent a user story or an implementation plan. Someone still decides those values; the change is that one command writes them and checks them. It does not make a story launchable that the existing rules block. If confirmed, the synthesis would assert this design. There is no leftover next-build.

5. Check before write. Each given value is checked with the existing story-quality predicate for its field. If a value fails, the command writes nothing and prints that predicate's message.
6. Keep what is there. An input that is not given leaves the existing value unchanged.
7. Two lists. After the write, the command prints the missing fields and the blocked conditions as separate lists, and says that no missing field does not mean the story can launch.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Given a freshly ingested story brief with no `plan.metadata.kind`, when `swarm:readiness --scaffold` runs with the required inputs, then it writes `kind: story` and does not refuse.
- Given a brief that has child plan references, when the scaffold command runs, then it refuses as today.
- Given explicit values for Description, UserStory, ImplementationPlan and Traces that pass the existing rules, when the scaffold command runs, then the brief holds those values.
- Given a UserStory value that does not match the existing pattern, when the scaffold command runs, then nothing is written and the existing message is printed.
- Given an item with no acceptance line and a clause keyed to its id, when the scaffold command runs, then the item acceptance line equals the clause text.
- Given a brief whose Overview names a file path and a shell command, when the scaffold command runs without `--file-scope` or `--verify-command`, then it refuses as today and writes neither.
- Given a brief with existing `expected_outputs`, when the scaffold command runs without that input, then the existing value is unchanged.
- Given one scaffold run that supplies every required value on a freshly ingested story brief, when `task swarm:readiness` runs, then it reports no missing field.
- Given a large story with `parallel_safe` false and every field filled, when `task swarm:readiness` runs, then it reports no missing field and still reports the story as blocked.
- Given a scaffold run, then its output lists missing fields and blocked conditions separately.

## Reject
- Deriving UserStory, ImplementationPlan, expected outputs, a conflict group or traces from issue text or by a template (comment 6908103663 finding 3).
- Treating text that ingest copied into the brief as a trusted source for paths or commands (comment 6908103663 finding 2).
- Promising a clean readiness result from filled fields (comment 6908103663 finding 1).
- Writing a longer Description at ingest from the issue body.
- Any change to a story-quality or readiness rule.
- A new command, gate or approval.

### 1. blocks-the-design — Check-before-write conflicts with complete-but-blocked authoring

## In plain English
Problem: after ingest, a brief cannot be launched until a user story, an implementation plan, an acceptance line per item, traces and a block of swarm fields are filled. No command writes most of them, so they are filled by hand edit or by a script in a separate pull request. The one command that writes part of the swarm block refuses a freshly ingested brief, because ingest does not record that the brief is a story.

What the critics found: most of these fields are decisions and cannot be derived from the issue. Issue text does not become trusted because ingest copied it into the brief. Filled fields do not make a story launchable. The first lean then failed its audit on two points: it stopped the write when a value failed a quality rule, which would block the complete-but-not-launchable stories it promised to support, and it addressed items by an id that ingest does not always give.

Solution this lean proposes: one command writes every launch field, and every value has a named source. The existing scaffold command gains inputs for the fields it cannot write today. Each value is either named by the operator on that command, or already on the brief. Two things are copied without being named: the story kind, when the brief is plainly a story, and an item's acceptance line, from the clause that already belongs to that item. Paths, commands and the other fields that give authority are never read from issue text or from text that ingest copied. The command writes what it is given, as it does today, and then reports missing fields and blocked conditions as two separate lists. An item is addressed by its id or by its position in the list.

What this adds: more inputs on one existing command. It adds no gate, refusal, approval or stop, and no check at write time.

What it removes: the hand edit or script for the launch fields, and the refusal of a freshly ingested brief by the scaffold command.

What it does not do: it does not invent a user story or an implementation plan. Someone still decides those values. A value that breaks a quality rule is written and then listed as a blocked condition, as `swarm:readiness` lists it today. It does not make a story launchable that the existing rules block. If confirmed, the synthesis would assert this design. There is no leftover next-build.

metadata.issueBody:
## Summary

An ingested brief arrives without the fields that launch needs, and its Description is only the issue title. Every story of wave 2a (nine briefs, 2026-11-15) needed these filled by hand before `swarm:launch`. This is split out of #6333 by operator decision (2026-11-16); #6333 keeps the acceptance-criteria part.

## What we saw

- After `issue:ingest`, `kind`, UserStory, ImplementationPlan, `items[].narrative.Acceptance` and the swarm block (readiness, parallel_safe, verify_commands, expected_outputs, depends_on, conflict_group, size, model_tier, Traces) are empty.
- Description is the title, which fails the story-quality rule (two sentences and at least 20 words).
- The pain-audit on #6333 (comment 6907314817, finding 3) found that the existing readiness scaffold does not write the narratives or Traces, needs file scope and verification commands as explicit inputs, and refuses commands taken from issue-body text.

## Expected

Fewer steps: ingest or promote writes every launch field that can be derived from a trusted input, and asks only for the operator-owned fields. No new gate or refusal.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Each launch field has a named writer and a named trusted input.
- Given an ingested and promoted brief with `size`, `parallel_safe` and `model_tier` set, when `task swarm:readiness` runs, then it reports no missing field.
- Given an ingested brief, then its Description passes the existing story-quality Description rule.
- Given an ingested brief, then no verification command is taken from untrusted issue-body text.
- No existing story-quality or readiness rule is weakened.

Refs #6333.

acceptance.derived_reason: one clause per harvested lean item (18), in list order (#6333)
sentences: Story kind. When `plan.metadata.kind` is absent and `kindOf` infers `story`, `swarm:readiness --scaffold` writes `kind: story` and proceeds. It still refuses an explicit or inferred epic or phase.

Narrative inputs. The scaffold command accepts explicit values for Description, UserStory, ImplementationPlan, Traces or the missing-traces justification, the acceptance-count justification, and an acceptance line per item. It accepts them as flags or as one values file that the operator names.
Item addressing. An item acceptance input names the item by its id or by its one-based position in `plan.items`. The command does not assign or change item ids.

Item acceptance copy. When an item has an id, has no acceptance line, and no explicit line is given, the command copies the text of the acceptance clause keyed to that id. It copies nothing else from brief text.

Authority fields. `file_scope`, `verify_commands`, `file_scope_confidence`, `size`, `parallel_safe`, `model_tier`, `readiness`, `expected_outputs`, `depends_on` and `conflict_group` are written only from an explicit input or kept from the value already on the brief. No path, command or other value for these fields is read from Overview, item titles, narratives or the issue.

Write, then report. The command writes the given values without a quality check, as it does today. An input that is not given leaves the existing value unchanged. After the write it runs the existing readiness evaluation on that brief and prints the missing fields and the blocked conditions as separate lists, and says that no missing field does not mean the story can launch.
Given a freshly ingested story brief with no `plan.metadata.kind`, when `swarm:readiness --scaffold` runs with the required inputs, then it writes `kind: story` and does not refuse.
Given a brief that has child plan references, when the scaffold command runs, then it refuses as today.
Given explicit values for Description, UserStory, ImplementationPlan and Traces, when the scaffold command runs, then the brief holds those values.
Given a UserStory value that does not match the existing pattern, when the scaffold command runs, then the value is written and the output lists the existing UserStory message as a blocked condition.
Given an item with no id, when the scaffold command is given an acceptance line for its position, then that item holds the line.
Given an item with an id, no acceptance line and a clause keyed to that id, when the scaffold command runs with no line for it, then the item acceptance line equals the clause text.
Given a scaffold run, then no item id is added or changed.
Given a brief whose Overview names a file path and a shell command, when the scaffold command runs without `--file-scope` or `--verify-command`, then it refuses as today and writes neither.
Given a brief with existing `expected_outputs`, when the scaffold command runs without that input, then the existing value is unchanged.
Given one scaffold run that supplies every required value on a freshly ingested story brief, when `task swarm:readiness` runs, then it reports no missing field.

Given a large story with `parallel_safe` false, readiness `ready` and every field supplied, when the scaffold command runs, then the values are written, no field is listed as missing, and the story is listed as blocked.
Given a scaffold run, then its output lists missing fields and blocked conditions separately.
Given a `file_scope` that touches a declared evaluator surface, when `file_scope` is written, then it includes `xbrief/evaluator-surface-disposition.json`.
Given a `file_scope` that touches no declared evaluator surface, when `file_scope` is written, then that path is not added.
Given a `file_scope` that already lists the path, when `file_scope` is written, then the path appears once.
